title: Plan card sorts and tree tests
summary: Keep grouping, findability and their analysis paths separate.
steps: For a card sort, define the grouping question, audience, understandable card set and open, closed or hybrid format.
Preserve original participant labels; document normalization, merge rules and denominators for co-placement. Coefficients and dendrograms suggest structures to test, not proven navigation.
For a tree test, version the trees, write neutral scenarios and define all accepted destinations and scoring before fielding.
Define direct success, first branch, backtracking and timing separately. Keep perceived success separate from recorded destination success.
Preserve participant pairing or task clustering and plan multiple comparisons. Lostness is optional and needs a valid definition and path data.
Test the resulting interface with a method that addresses remaining usability and accessibility questions.
questions: Am I measuring grouping or findability?
Does the task wording disclose a destination label?
example: Ask where someone would find a past notice, without repeating the navigation label that is the intended destination.
